proposed_statement_changes.reason: After removal of the supplied rational realization and supplied graph family as domain assumptions, the old universal two-output claim is too strong because it presupposes a nonempty oracle model and a nonempty graph family. The replacement narrows causal-output guarantees to the explicitly nonempty case, adds exact rejection certificates otherwise, drops all complexity and height promises, and within the valid case reports the directive's maximal effect quotient.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The tied minimum-edge family must be constructed completely from the finite vertex set, background orientations, and exact CI oracle; a supplied SA-MPDAG or CPDAG representation is only an optional validated compression.

Realizability and existence of an admissible DAG are now decided by the algorithm. A rational table and compressed graph family can be optional checked accelerators but cannot remain mathematical acceptance assumptions.

The corrected procedure must decide model nonemptiness, enumerate all admissible minimum-edge ties by default, and compute the full pairwise effect quotient with equality and positive-separator certificates.

prose_updates.tldr: SparseSIM-ID no longer assumes a supplied positive rational realization or a supplied complete graph family. From a finite exact CI oracle and background orientations it first certifies oracle realizability, exhaustively constructs every minimum-edge DAG I-map unless a valid compressed certificate is supplied, and computes the unique coarsest quotient of the tied family whose classes share the same \(P_x(Y)\) functional on the strictly positive exact-oracle model. It returns one observable circuit per class, exact within-class equality certificates, and an exact real-algebraic positive ambiguity table for every class pair. Normalization reduces the full pairwise feasibility count to \(\binom{|\mathfrak D|}{2}(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\); the one-reference common-effect test uses \((|\mathfrak D|-1)(\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|-1)\). The four-binary-variable rational witness and fixed-circuit plug-in inference are preserved.

project_justification.gap: Existing simultaneous-identification criteria are sufficient graphical tests and do not compute the maximal law-restricted effect quotient across all tied minimum-edge DAG I-maps. Saturated CI ideals also do not select strict positivity or the bit-zero exact-oracle chamber.
project_justification.niche: For finite observed variables, the exact oracle, all admissible DAGs, every graphwise truncated functional, and every positive-chamber equality test are finite and exact. This makes the tied-sparsest family itself computable and supports a graph-native maximal quotient rather than arbitrary selection of one tie.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a terminating realizability-first algorithm that enumerates all minimum-edge I-map ties, partitions them by universal equality of their causal distributions on the strictly positive exact-oracle model, and certifies every merge or separation. It exposes reduced reference and all-pairs decision counts, preserves real-radical zero tests only as an optional fast equality branch, and returns algebraic-number ambiguity witnesses whenever classes differ.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from one fixed strictly positive multinomial law \(P\) after a real-realizable exact oracle, its computed tied family, and one returned effect class have been fixed; a common-effect analysis uses the one-class case.

prose_updates.related_work: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025, Theorem 3.2 and Section 4.2) give the closest simultaneous-identification boundary: their SA-MPDAG condition is sufficient, whereas SparseSIM-ID decides and certifies the complete effect quotient of every finite tied minimum-edge I-map family. The preserved four-node rational example lies outside that graphical sufficient region and has two distinct causal values. Perkovic (2020, Theorem 3.6) supplies single-MPDAG identification structure, but no extensional equivalence with the present law-restricted cross-family quotient is claimed. Guo and Perkovic (2021, Theorem 3) minimally enumerate graph-generic effect functionals within one MPDAG; the proved relation is one-way: a class they certify as one functional is contained in a SparseSIM-ID class whenever the exact-oracle model is contained in that MPDAG's positive Markov model. Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005) inform saturation, while Tarski's decision method and Stengle's Positivstellensatz provide supporting exact feasibility machinery rather than the causal novelty. Kahle, Rauh, and Sullivant (2017) explain why irrelevant CI components preclude reading positive exact-oracle separation from ideal nonmembership. Raskutti and Uhler (2018) motivate retention of all sparsest ties; the new output policy quotients those ties by the causal query. Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019), Duarte et al. (2024), and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024) remain adjacent completeness, optimization, and post-selection comparators rather than equivalent results.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Termination and the numbers of positive-chamber comparisons are explicit, but no favorable running-time, degree, certificate-length, or algebraic-height bound is claimed. The default DAG enumeration is finite and may be exponential or worse. Saturation by cells and denominators excludes components contained in their zero sets but imposes neither positivity nor bit-zero nonvanishing, so a nonzero normal form is only a feasibility trigger. General feasible separators are guaranteed to be exact real algebraic, not rational. The remaining rational-output question asks only whether an actually feasible set \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\{F_{D,D',y}\neq0\}\) always contains a bounded-height rational point; it is not needed for correctness or completeness of the decision theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The required inputs are finite state spaces, a complete exact CI bit-vector, background orientations, and a query. A rational realization and a compressed SA-MPDAG or CPDAG family are optional checked accelerators, not assumptions. Unrealizable exact oracles and background systems admitting no I-map receive finite rejection certificates; every real-realizable oracle with at least one admissible DAG proceeds to the complete tied minimum-edge quotient. Separators are exact real algebraic unless an optional rational sample succeeds, and no polynomial-time or uniform height guarantee is made. The quotient is law-restricted and can be coarser than a graph-generic within-MPDAG enumeration; only the proved one-way Guo--Perkovic containment is claimed. The four-variable table remains an explicit rational cross-MEC separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). Plug-in inference is pointwise for a fixed returned circuit and is not selection-aware inference for an estimated oracle or tie family.

statement_notes.justification: This is the graph-native contribution: a finite realizability-first construction of the unique maximal effect quotient, with one representative circuit per class and exact certificates for every merge and separation.
statement_notes.gap: Sufficient graphical tests do not decide equality on the exact positive law chamber, and selecting one tied graph discards both common-effect and ambiguity information.
statement_notes.consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP can report the complete class structure, a single common circuit when there is one class, or exact positive ambiguity tables when there are several.

statement_notes.justification: The positive-chamber decision is supporting finite semialgebraic machinery used to certify one graph-pair coordinate; it is not the causal novelty and does not promise a rational witness.
statement_notes.gap: Saturation alone does not select the positive exact-oracle chamber, so each nonzero normal form must be followed by an actual feasibility decision.
statement_notes.consumer: The maximal-quotient algorithm obtains an exactly checkable algebraic sample or infeasibility identity for each unresolved coordinate.

statement_notes.justification: The corollary records uniqueness of the quotient and the exact one-way relation to within-MPDAG minimal enumeration without asserting an unproved equivalence.
statement_notes.gap: Graph-generic functional equality and equality restricted to one exact-oracle model need not coincide.
statement_notes.consumer: Implementers can safely reuse a Guo--Perkovic merge while allowing SparseSIM-ID to certify additional law-specific merges.

statement_notes.justification: The rational-witness question is an optional arithmetic refinement of a feasible positive chamber, not a prerequisite for the proved semialgebraic decision or maximal quotient.
statement_notes.gap: A nonempty rationally defined semialgebraic set on a conditional-independence variety can have algebraic points without an established bounded-height rational point theorem.
statement_notes.consumer: A positive answer would replace some algebraic separator encodings by bounded-height rational tables; a negative answer would leave the complete algebraic-number output unchanged.
